<reason>A built the cleaner theory — the "prophecy gate" frame and the person-judgment vs. idea-judgment distinction in A1 were the debate's best single answer, and A's Q1 genuinely damaged B's Karikó exhibit. But B's core route survived intact and grew sharper: competition as many small, reversible, appealable, visible decisions versus block grants as one early biography-based judgment with no exit. A answered "who picks the explorers" but never addressed the mid-career outsider the institution writes off, nor B's point that plural panels restore the tail A claimed consensus destroys. B's implicit-prophecy flip ("her next decade will resemble her last") muddied A's frame, and B's closing confronted the live clash more completely while A's closing left the exit and redundancy points standing. A's Rebuttal 2 clipping was a real execution cost. B also converted the motion's accountability concession into an error-correction argument rather than mere bean-counting, giving the cleaner reason to vote against the motion as written.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B2.1's pounce on A2.1 ("the same people who pick them now" = testing a biography at thirty-two and stopping) plus the unanswered institutional-sovereignty point in B4.1–B4.3: under block grants the department that demoted Karikó becomes her last door, and the outsider disappears inside the institutional average reviewers actually score.</best_rebuttal>
